newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up at 19-month high.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up at 19-month high.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Saturday for the fifth straight day of gain at 19-month high as sentiment turned bullish after recent gains set this year's new high since Thursday, brokers said.

"Fundamental improvement also backed up the rises," said Michael Hung of Nikko Securities. "After seeing recovery in the personal computer and construction industries, we now see some gradual recovery in the textile and plastic industries."
The index ended up 28.45 points or 0.43 percent at 6,644.66, the highest since February 18, 1995.
Turnover was an active T$48.45 billion.
Electronics, after recent gains, encountered profit-taking in early trade, but late buying pushed up the sector again, rising 1.19 percent, with Mosel up 60 cents to T$37.9.
"Electronics had performed well in the third quarter, and they are expected to perform even better in the fourth quarter," Hung said.
Constructions, financials and steels also rose, but plastics fell. Long Bond Construction rose T$1.1 to T$31.7.
Brokers said Saturday's government announcement of a stable 3.84 percent year-on-year growth in September consumer prices should help maintain a loose monetary policy.
Brokers said the index may consolidate next week within a 6,550-6,750 range in a cautious response after recent rises.
"But a firming trend is seen in the mid-term, with the index likely to test 7,000 points by December," Hung said.
